meta.title: Mia's Fact File: The Gibbon
meta.textType: functional: a fact file with headings, a blog post

paragraphs: Posted by Mia. Mia's Fact File: The Gibbon On Saturday, September fifth, the Explorers visited the small zoo. Lily, Leo, and Teacher Kim came with me, and I took my camera. A sign by the fence said, "Gibbons." A gibbon sat high in a tree. I pointed my camera at it. Teacher Kim reads each post first, and then she puts it on the blog.

The gibbon was swinging between two ropes when I took my first photo. It used its long arms, and it moved very fast. Leo laughed and said, "It looks like a monkey!" "It is an ape, not a monkey," I said. "An ape has no tail." Lily asked, "What is a gibbon like?" "It is small, fast, and noisy," I said. Then I decided to write a fact file. My fact file has four headings. They are "Where gibbons live," "What gibbons eat," "How gibbons move," and "Fast facts."

Where gibbons live Gibbons live in the rainforest. It is their natural home. They live where the trees are tall and the air is warm. Some gibbons also live in the mountains. A gibbon sleeps high in a tree. What gibbons eat Gibbons eat fruit, leaves, and insects. They find most of their food in the high trees.

How gibbons move A gibbon swings from tree to tree with its long arms. Its arms are longer than its legs. It is not heavy, so it can swing very fast. Gibbons almost never come down to the ground. Fast facts An adult gibbon is bigger than a cat, but lighter than a child. Gibbons are noisy, especially in the morning. You can hear them from far away in the rainforest.
I like gibbons because they are fast and funny. Do you like gibbons? Which animal do you like? Please tell us in the comments.
